one_liner: Closed-source NVMe KV engine (UDisk) behind UStore's open C API; vendor numbers show 2-7x RocksDB throughput.
what_it_does: UStore (formerly UKV) is an Apache-2.0 C99 interface, with C++17, Python, Go and Java SDKs and an Arrow Flight server, that stores blob, document, graph and vector collections on interchangeable engines: UCSet (in-memory), LevelDB, RocksDB and UDisk. The API is not RocksDB's: each call takes one struct of strided key/value arrays, keys are signed 64-bit integers, values are capped at 4 GB, and output memory comes from arenas UStore owns. The speedup in this entry belongs to UDisk, a persistent transactional engine that Unum ships only as a prebuilt static library; the open repo holds the adapters and bindings, not UDisk itself.
how_it_is_fast: Unum describes UDisk as a modified LSM tree built for NVMe block devices, with io_uring for partial kernel bypass, SPDK for full bypass, a custom internal filesystem and optional CUDA offload of background compactions. Its config offers posix, 'pulling' and 'polling' IO mechanisms with queue depths up to 4096, native fixed-size integer keys and optional fixed-size values. Batch reads go in as a group so the engine can reorder them and issue them asynchronously, which is where the widest gap over RocksDB's MultiGet shows up; none of this can be checked, because the source is closed.
when_to_use: You have, or can negotiate, a UDisk binary from Unum and run Linux servers with several NVMe drives, where batched random reads and upserts of values around 1 KB dominate.

Keys are naturally 64-bit integers (row IDs, graph vertex IDs) and you can send batches of hundreds of keys per call instead of single Gets; batch read is the vendor's largest win (650K vs 4.5M ops/s).

You want one transactional C API over blobs, documents and graphs, with NetworkX- and Pandas-style Python front ends. You can start on the open UCSet or RocksDB engines and swap in UDisk later without changing application code.
when_not_to_use: You need an engine you can build, audit or patch: UDisk is binary-only, and UStore's own engine table marks it as not open source.
Range-select-heavy workloads: in the vendor's own 10 TB run RocksDB did 5M ops/s against 2M for UDisk (then called UnumDB), and the README table leaves that row out.

Non-Linux targets, or code that relies on RocksDB features such as string keys with custom comparators, prefix seeks and column-family options. UDisk is Linux-only and links liburing, libnuma and libexplain.
You need durable writes by default. UStore turns durability off unless you pass ustore_option_write_flush_k, and its RocksDB adapter sets disableWAL whenever that flag is missing.
Production systems that need a live upstream: main was last committed 2023-08-18, and open bugs include the README's rocksdb.DataBase('/path') example failing to open (#434).

integration.form: static lib (CMake builds ustore_embedded_<engine> static libraries; UDisk is a prebuilt static archive passed in through USTORE_ENGINE_UDISK_PATH)
integration.dependencies: UStore: Apache Arrow (plus Flight and Parquet), simdjson, yyjson, mongo-c-driver (BSON), PCRE2, fmt, mpack, nlohmann/json; optional jemalloc, oneTBB, Boost, OpenSSL. UDisk adds liburing, libnuma, libexplain, libdl and pthread.
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 and CMake 3.16+ (C99 for the C headers); no minimum compiler version documented
integration.platforms: UDisk: Linux only. UStore: Linux; the roadmap lists Arm and macOS builds as done. x86 builds hard-code -msse4.2 -mavx2 in CMake. PyPI 'ukv' 0.12.1 ships only manylinux x86_64 wheels for CPython 3.9 and 3.10.
integration.thread_safety: Per db.h, a database handle can be shared across threads between open and free. Transaction handles are not thread-safe and use optimistic concurrency control, and only one process may open an embedded database directory. UDisk caps concurrent accessor threads with its concurrency_limit setting.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — UStore can wrap RocksDB itself (as an OptimisticTransactionDB) behind its own API. Moving to UDisk still means adopting the ustore_* C API with integer keys; there is no RocksDB-compatible API and no support for RocksDB options files.

gotchas: The December 2022 table matches Unum's September 2022 10 TB post row for row except Batch Upsert. The post gives UDisk 117K ops/s on CPU and 182K with a GPU, not 260K, so no published run backs the ~4.6x upsert figure. The table also leaves out Initialization (603K vs 60M) and Range Select, where RocksDB won.

The setup favored UDisk. In the post each engine got 8 SSD partitions, but RocksDB can take at most 4 db_paths and ingested SSTs land on the first disk. The UCSB RocksDB adapter runs with the WAL disabled. In the earlier single-threaded 1 TB run the gaps were much smaller: random reads 175.7K vs 160.7K (~1.1x), batch insert 813K vs 690K (~1.2x).

Reproduction is blocked even with a binary. UCSB's cmake/ustore.cmake clones a 'main-dev' branch that no longer exists and passes -DUSTORE_ENGINE_NAME_UDISK_PATH, while UStore's CMake reads USTORE_ENGINE_UDISK_PATH. UCSB also has no license, and its committed RocksDB 10TB.cfg says 7.2.9 while the post says 6.29.3.

The PyPI package is 'ukv' (imported as ustore.*), not 'ustore'; issue #383 shows users confused by the ukv/ustore/ucset naming. Per #434, opening RocksDB works only when you pass a JSON config with create_if_missing, not a bare path.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick UDisk only if you have a commercial path to the binary and a batch-heavy, integer-keyed workload on Linux machines with several NVMe drives; for an engine you can build and audit, SplinterDB (6-10x faster inserts and 2-2.6x faster point queries than RocksDB), KVell or F2 (FASTER) have open code and better evidence. UStore's open parts only beat them if you want its multi-modal API over RocksDB or UCSet, not for speed.
verified_claims_summary: These are vendor-run UCSB numbers: apart from Batch Upsert, the README rows match Unum's September 2022 10 TB run of RocksDB 6.29.3 against UDisk (then 'UnumDB'), with 8-byte integer keys, 1 KB values, compression off, no flushing, 64 client threads and 256-key batches on an AMD Threadripper PRO 3995WX with 1 TB RAM, 8x Samsung PM1733 NVMe and Ubuntu 22.04 (kernel 5.15, ext4); no compiler is stated, and the README table gives no setup at all. Under those conditions batch reads ran ~6.9x and point reads ~2.4x faster, scans tied, and RocksDB won range selects ~2.5x.
status_note: Abandoned: main (the only branch) was last committed 2023-08-18 at v0.13.12, and neither UStore nor the placeholder UDisk repo links a public UDisk download, so the Apache-2.0 bindings still work with RocksDB, LevelDB and UCSet but the engine this entry measures is out of reach.
